script.base: Tampa Bay is a 4.5-point home favorite in an outdoor 1:00 ET kick, total 44.5, so the book prices a one-score game with TB at 24.5 and Arizona at 20.0, not a blowout and not a shootout. TB should lead late and lean on the run it has actually used in weeks 10-12: Sean Tucker 40 carries for 201 yards (5.0 YPC) and Rachaad White 27 for 127, with Baker Mayfield (Questionable, shoulder) assumed to start but not trusted for a 30-point script. Arizona cannot run it: Trey Benson is Out, Emari Demercado is Out, Bam Knight is Questionable and has 25 carries for only 64 yards (2.56 YPC) over those three weeks, and the line is missing Will Hernandez and Christian Jones. Jacoby Brissett (9 rushes, 49 yards in that window) will throw to stay within 4.5, and the ball has gone to Trey McBride (34 targets, 321 yards, 226 air) and Michael Wilson (prop last4 61, 34, 185, 118; target table Mi.Wilson 29 targets, 262 yards, 311 air).
script.flip1: TB scores early and leads by 10-14. Arizona abandons Knight and Michael Carter (L3 10 carries, 38 yards), pass volume rises, and McBride/Wilson targets go up if drives survive. TB clocks it with Tucker and White. A true blowout is the less likely branch of this flip because the spread is only 4.5, so starter snap risk is moderate, not base.
script.flip2: Mayfield sits or cannot push the ball with the shoulder, or Arizona's defense (even without DT Walter Nolen and S Dadrion Taylor-Demerson) holds TB under 24.5 and Arizona leads. Then Arizona can run with Carter or a limited Knight, McBride and Wilson volume falls, and Egbuka/Otton/Shepard/Tez lines depend on a backup the pack does not name. Unsaved outdoor weather is the other version of this flip: a slog under 44.5.

pre_mortem: Monday both overs lost because Tampa Bay spent the week on the only two Arizona skill players with real target shares, the 38% blitz and the Hernandez/Jones replacements turned Brissett into a checkdown quarterback, and the 127/115 and 185/118 games were the outliers. McBride finished in the 55-yard bin, Wilson finished at 34, Mayfield played well enough that Arizona never had to throw 35 times, and the median stand-in numbers were never soft market prices. That case is why Wilson is a lean and why neither leg is sized. It is not stronger than three straight McBride clears into a 9.36 middle YPA with both linebackers questionable, so McBride stays a strong read and is flagged, not cut.
